title: Protocol translation gateway: behavioral delta remediation for OpenAI Responses mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We are seeing multiple behavioral divergences between incoming OpenAI 'Responses' API traffic and Redwood's native event model (streaming chunks, semantic tool_call vs function_call, structured output enforcement, token boundary markers). This ticket scopes a lightweight runtime 'translation gateway' that normalizes incoming OpenAI-style events into Redwood's canonical protocol at the edge, provides feature-flagged fallbacks, and ships a set of deterministic heuristics for resolving parity gaps without changing customer prompts. Goal: reduce customer-visible parity regressions for streaming+tool-calling workloads by 80% for the initial canary cohort and provide an operational plan for rollout to Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Translation gateway deploys as a sidecar at the routing layer and accepts OpenAI Responses event stream payloads and HTTP responses
Streaming deltas are rehydrated into Redwood token events with preserved ordering and stable token-ids so downstream runtimes can apply KV-cache and batching without divergence
Tool/function call semantics are normalized: gateway emits explicit 'tool_call_start', 'tool_call_args', 'tool_call_end' events for OpenAI 'tool_call' and 'function_call' variants

Structured outputs (application/json, json-schema hints) are validated by the gateway with a configurable strictness level; failures are emitted as a standardized StructuredOutputWarning event and downstream receives a fallback text path
Canary runs produce telemetry demonstrating reduced mismatches (diff rate <= 20%) against a baseline harness across 5 representative customer prompts
Automated test suite (unit + integration) covering streaming reassembly, toolcall mapping, stop-sequence handling, and schema enforcement is checked into CI
Rollout playbook and rollback steps are documented in the linked design doc
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, API, and Console owners. Captured behavioral diff catalog and initial priority scenarios (streaming partial content, nested toolcalls, JSON-lines structured output).

2025-02-14: Prototype gateway implemented in Rust; basic reassembly of 'delta' type chunks into canonical token events tested locally. Proof-of-concept PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2783

2025-02-20: PM/Design review - agreed on non-destructive normalization (no content mangling) and a flag to preserve raw OpenAI payloads for debugging. Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/OA+Resp+Translation+Gateway
2025-02-25: Discovered edge-case: OpenAI emits function_call with partial args across stream frames; added rehydration buffer and idempotency checks in gateway prototype
2025-03-01: Integration tests added against eval harness (responses-interop-harness); observed 72% reduction in observable downstream schema errors for structured-output scenarios.
2025-03-05: Ready for canary in staging - feature-flag gated. Next: run 48h canary against 3 low-impact customers and collect telemetry.
decisions: Implement translation gateway as edge-side service (sidecar) rather than changing core serving runtime to minimize blast radius and to allow per-customer toggles
Favor heuristic normalization with explicit warnings over silent content rewriting; provide opt-in strict mode that enforces JSON schema and rejects non-conforming outputs
Expose a runtime compatibility flag 'oa_responses_mode' per-route that toggles gateway behavior (lenient | strict | passthrough)
Do not attempt to emulate OpenAI internal streaming token ids; instead generate stable Redwood token ids and map OpenAI token offsets into metadata for observability
risks: Latency regression at the edge if reassembly logic induces synchronous waits; mitigation: implement streaming pipelined processing and backpressure-aware buffers
Behavioral mismatches may still surface for complex, nested tool-calling patterns; mitigation: maintain a catalog of 'unmappable' patterns and fallback to passthrough mode
Customer confusion if gateway modifies output shape unexpectedly; mitigation: structuredOutputWarning events, opt-out, and detailed changelog for canary participants
Security: validating arbitrary JSON from tool outputs could introduce DoS parsing vectors; mitigation: size/time limits and defensive parsing library selection (serde with timeouts)
monitoring_metrics: openai_diff_rate_percent (percent of messages with behavioral differences detected)
notes: This ticket focuses strictly on protocol-level normalization; any semantic reranking or output rewriting to match exact tokenization/penalty behavior is out of scope and should be handled by a follow-up project.
Coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer-facing release notes and guidance for prompt authors when canary begins.
Keep gateway logs compact; include a hashed payload fingerprint for debugging rather than full PII content
